chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) in
a woman said to a man: 'The private part of your slave girl is lawful for you,' so he had intercourse with her, and she bore a child; the child's value is assessed against him.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a child born from a slave girl when the man claims her private part is lawful for him?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s chain in *al-Istibsar* clarifies the fiqh of *tahlil* (temporary marriage for divorce purposes) specifically regarding slave girls, establishing that the child born is considered *walad al-mubarad* (child of the master) and entitles the mother to financial compensation (*qimah*) upon the master's death or as a specific ruling. It highlights the Shia juristic view on the economic rights of slave mothers in this context, distinguishing it from free women, and underscores the practical application of lineage and manumission rules in early Islamic society.
